content</a>\n<header class=\"top\">\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <p class=\"eyebrow\">Explorable companion to the paper</p>\n    <h1 id=\"title\">Peer Agreement as a Reference-Free Signal of NL→FOL Faithfulness, and Where It Fails</h1>\n    <p class=\"byline\">The paper gives no author line. Every chart below is computed in your browser from the run's recorded outputs.</p>\n    <ul class=\"links\" aria-label=\"Paper links\">\n      <li><a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a></li>\n      <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a></li>\n      <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the\">Code repository</a></li>\n    </ul>\n  </div>\n</header>\n<nav class=\"sections\" aria-label=\"Sections\">\n  <ul>\n    <li><a href=\"#finding\">The finding</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#how\">How it works</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#evidence\">Explore the evidence</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#try\">Try it</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#fails\">Where it fails</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#notes\">Links, data, glossary</a></li>\n  </ul>\n</nav>\n\n<main id=\"main\" tabindex=\"-1\">\n\n<!-- ============================================================ FINDING -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"finding\" aria-labelledby=\"h-finding\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <div class=\"grid2\">\n    <div class=\"prose\">\n      <h2 id=\"h-finding\">The finding</h2>\n      <p class=\"lede\">Can you tell whether a first-order logic formula says what its sentence says, with no gold formula and without reading the sentence at all?</p>\n      <p>Correct FOL is not unique, and benchmark gold is often wrong. The paper asks whether the other systems can serve as the reference. Nine current LLMs formalize the same sentence. An SMT solver checks which of their formulas are logically equivalent after a <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"align\">vocabulary alignment that never reads predicate names</button>. A candidate's <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"pa\">peer agreement score</button> is the reliability-weighted share of peers equivalent to it.</p>\n      <p>On 450 fresh sentences, frozen before any label existed, the answer is yes for short benchmark text:</p>\n      <div class=\"bignum\" aria-live=\"polite\">\n        <div><div class=\"n ours\" id=\"big-pa\">&nbsp;</div><div class=\"l\">peer agreement <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"auroc\">AUROC</button>, <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"panel\">panel labels</button></div></div>\n        <div><div class=\"n base\" id=\"big-judge\">&nbsp;</div><div class=\"l\"><button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"judge\">LLM judge</button> (gemini-2.5-flash), same items</div></div>\n      </div>\n      <p>Under <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"solver\">audited solver labels</button> the gap widens to 0.874 against 0.727. The gain it adds on top of a judge is small, though: about +0.03 AUROC on panel labels, with an interval that touches zero. It ties an existing <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"dsbin\">Dawid–Skene agreement</button> estimator, and it falls below chance when most systems share an error.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-head\" style=\"margin-top:0\">\n      <p class=\"q\">Does peer agreement beat the judge under both label families, and on every corpus?</p>\n      <div class=\"controls\">\n        <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-head-fam\">Label family</span>\n          <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-head-fam\" id=\"head-fam\">\n            <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"P\">Panel (256)</button>\n            <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"S\">Solver (3,720)</button>\n          </div></div>\n        <label>Corpus<select id=\"head-corpus\"><option value=\"all\">All three</option><option value=\"malls\">MALLS</option><option value=\"folio\">FOLIO v2 train</option><option value=\"proverqa\">ProverQA</option></select></label>\n        <label>Complexity tercile<select id=\"head-terc\"><option value=\"all\">All</option><option value=\"bottom\">Bottom</option><option value=\"middle\">Middle</option><option value=\"top\">Top</option></select></label>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"legend\"><span style=\"--c:var(--accent)\">Peer agreement (the paper's score)</span><span style=\"--c:var(--base)\">LLM judge (baseline)</span><span style=\"--c:var(--other)\">Other scores</span></div>\n      <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-head\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"AUROC by score\"></div>\n      <p class=\"note\" id=\"head-note\"></p>\n      <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"head-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================================================ HOW -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"how\" aria-labelledby=\"h-how\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-how\">How it works</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\">\n    <p class=\"q\">What happens between nine formulas and one score?</p>\n    <p>Walk one real sentence from the fresh set through the six stages. Every value shown is what the run recorded: the systems' outputs, the maps the alignment search found, the solver's relations, the fitted weights and the final score. Choose which output plays the candidate; the others are its peers.</p>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"card view stepper\" id=\"stepper\" tabindex=\"0\" aria-label=\"Method stepper. Use the left and right arrow keys to move between stages.\">\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label>Candidate output<select id=\"st-cand\"></select></label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"pipe\" id=\"pipe\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\"></div>\n    <div id=\"st-live\" class=\"sr-only\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <div class=\"stage-body\" id=\"st-body\"></div>\n    <div class=\"stepnav\">\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"plain\" id=\"st-prev\">← Previous stage</button>\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"plain\" id=\"st-next\">Next stage →</button>\n      <span class=\"note\" id=\"st-count\"></span>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"st-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n  <figure>\n    <img src=\"figures/fig2_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Diagram of the peer agreement score: a candidate formula and eight peer formulas pass through a name-free alignment (bijection, then partial map), a Z3 relation per pair, equivalence clusters with one-coin Dawid-Skene weights, and a weighted share of EQUIV peers between 0 and 1; the sentence is not read by the score, and the gold can be scored as a tenth peer to flag wrong gold.\" loading=\"lazy\" width=\"3168\" height=\"1344\">\n    <figcaption>The paper's method figure. The peer agreement score. A candidate formula is compared with each peer formula (other systems' outputs for the same sentence) after a name-free vocabulary alignment (a bijection, then a partial map). An SMT solver decides the logical relation of each aligned pair. EQUIV relations define equivalence clusters, from which a label-free one-coin Dawid-Skene model estimates one reliability weight per system. The score is the weighted share of peers that are equivalent to the candidate. The sentence text and predicate names are never read.</figcaption>\n  </figure>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================================================ EVIDENCE -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"evidence\" aria-labelledby=\"h-ev\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-ev\">Explore the evidence</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\"><p>Three views over the recorded data: every one of the 4,050 fresh candidates, reliability as sentences get more complex, and a constructed test of vocabulary.</p></div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-browser\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Item browser</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">What does agreement see in one case that the judge misses, or the reverse?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label>Items<select id=\"b-set\"><option value=\"P\">Panel-labelled</option><option value=\"S\">Solver-labelled</option><option value=\"A\">All fresh candidates</option></select></label>\n      <label>Label<select id=\"b-lab\"><option value=\"any\">Any</option><option value=\"1\">Faithful</option><option value=\"0\">Unfaithful</option></select></label>\n      <label>System<select id=\"b-sys\"><option value=\"all\">All nine</option></select></label>\n      <label>Corpus<select id=\"b-corpus\"><option value=\"all\">All</option><option value=\"malls\">MALLS</option><option value=\"folio\">FOLIO v2 train</option><option value=\"proverqa\">ProverQA</option></select></label>\n      <label>Sort<select id=\"b-sort\"><option value=\"gapJ\">Judge far above agreement</option><option value=\"gapA\">Agreement far above judge</option><option value=\"lo\">Lowest agreement first</option><option value=\"hi\">Highest agreement first</option></select></label>\n      <label style=\"flex:1 1 220px\">Search sentence or formula<input type=\"search\" id=\"b-q\" placeholder=\"e.g. unless, student, ∃\"></label>\n      <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"b-dis\"> Only where the two scores disagree by 0.5 or more</label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"note\" id=\"b-count\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"browser\">\n      <div>\n        <ul class=\"ilist\" id=\"b-list\" aria-label=\"Matching items\"></ul>\n        <button type=\"button\" class=\"plain\" id=\"b-more\" style=\"margin-top:8px\">Show 50 more</button>\n      </div>\n      <div id=\"b-detail\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"b-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-cx\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Reliability as sentences get more complex</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">Does agreement keep its lead over the judge on longer, more nested, more quantified sentences?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label>Complexity feature<select id=\"cx-feat\"><option value=\"tok\">Sentence length (tokens)</option><option value=\"q\">Quantifiers</option><option value=\"nest\">Nesting depth</option><option value=\"cond\">Conditions</option><option value=\"terc\">Composite tercile</option></select></label>\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-cx-fam\">Label family</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-cx-fam\" id=\"cx-fam\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"P\">Panel</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"S\">Solver</button>\n        </div></div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span style=\"--c:var(--accent)\">Peer agreement</span><span style=\"--c:var(--base)\">LLM judge</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-cx\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"AUROC by complexity stratum\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"cx-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-vocab\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Renaming the predicates</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">If the same formulas are written with random tokens or synonyms instead of conventional names, which scores move?</p>\n    <p class=\"note\">Constructed test on 223 development sentences with faithful gold: each faithful formula against 739 operator <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"mutant\">mutants</button>, in four renderings. In the crossed rendering the faithful formula uses random tokens while its mutants keep conventional names.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-vo\">Rendering</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-vo\" id=\"vo-arm\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"conf\">Modal peer's names</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"tok\">Random tokens</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"syn\">WordNet synonyms</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"crossed\">Crossed</button>\n        </div></div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-vocab\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"AUROC by score for the selected rendering\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"vo-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================================================ TRY -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"try\" aria-labelledby=\"h-try\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-try\">Try it</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\"><p>The last stage of the method is plain arithmetic over the solver's recorded relations, so the page can run it exactly. The solver itself is not rerun here; its relations for every pair of the 450 fresh sentences are embedded.</p></div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-calc\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Recompute a score</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">How much does one candidate's score depend on which peers vote and how they are weighted?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label style=\"flex:1 1 320px\">Sentence (fresh set, with a panel label)<select id=\"k-sent\"></select></label>\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"plain\" id=\"k-rand\">Random sentence</button>\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-kw\">Weights</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-kw\" id=\"k-w\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"ds\">Dawid–Skene</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"uni\">Uniform</button>\n        </div></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"fol\" id=\"k-text\" style=\"font-family:var(--font);font-size:16px\"></p>\n    <div class=\"tscroll\"><table id=\"k-table\"><caption class=\"sr-only\">Outputs for the selected sentence. Pick the candidate and the peers that vote.</caption>\n      <thead><tr><th scope=\"col\">Candidate</th><th scope=\"col\">Peer votes</th><th scope=\"col\">System</th><th scope=\"col\" class=\"num\">Weight</th><th scope=\"col\">Formula</th><th scope=\"col\">Relation to candidate</th></tr></thead><tbody></tbody></table></div>\n    <div class=\"calc\" id=\"k-out\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"k-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-thr\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Use it as a filter</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">If you flag every output whose agreement falls below a threshold, how many bad formulas do you catch, and what does the judge catch at the same flag rate?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <div class=\"range\"><label for=\"t-range\" class=\"ctl-label\" style=\"flex-direction:row;align-items:center;gap:10px;color:var(--ink)\">Flag if peer agreement is below <output id=\"t-val\" for=\"t-range\" style=\"font-weight:700;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums\">0.50</output></label>\n        <input type=\"range\" id=\"t-range\" min=\"0\" max=\"1\" step=\"0.01\" value=\"0.5\"></div>\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-tf\">Label family</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-tf\" id=\"t-fam\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"P\">Panel</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"S\">Solver</button>\n        </div></div>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"stat\" id=\"t-stats\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <div class=\"legend\"><span style=\"--c:var(--accent)\">Peer agreement</span><span style=\"--c:var(--base)\">LLM judge</span></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-roc\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Catch rate against false-flag rate\"></div>\n    <p class=\"note\">Computed live from the recorded scores. Panel items carry their sampling weights; the judge's scores are coarse, so its matched flag rate is the closest one it can reach.</p>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"t-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============================================================ FAILS -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"fails\" aria-labelledby=\"h-fails\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-fails\">Where it fails</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\"><p>Agreement cannot see a mistake most peers make. The three views below show that boundary on fresh sentences, in a controlled dose test, and on long legal definitions.</p></div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-shared\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">When the majority is wrong</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">What happens to agreement on sentences whose <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"modal\">modal cluster</button> is unfaithful?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-sh\">Panel items in sentences where the modal cluster is</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-sh\" id=\"sh-split\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"all\">Any</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"ok\">Faithful</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"bad\">Unfaithful</button>\n        </div></div>\n      <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"sh-list\"> List the items agreement gets wrong here</label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-shared\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"AUROC in the selected split\"></div>\n    <p class=\"note\">The modal cluster's correctness is read from the labels of its members (panel labels first, else solver labels), so this split is descriptive.</p>\n    <div id=\"sh-items\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"sh-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-dose\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">The dose test</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">How many peers must share a mistake before agreement prefers the mistake?</p>\n    <p class=\"note\">200 development sentences, 560 items over four operators: <em>k</em> of the eight peers are replaced by renamed copies of a mutant. Detection is the probability that the faithful formula scores above the mutant.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <div class=\"ctl-label\"><span id=\"lab-do\">Peers replaced</span>\n        <div class=\"seg\" role=\"radiogroup\" aria-labelledby=\"lab-do\" id=\"do-order\">\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"true\" data-v=\"random\">In random order</button>\n          <button type=\"button\" role=\"radio\" aria-checked=\"false\" data-v=\"faithful_first\">Faithful peers first</button>\n        </div></div>\n      <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"do-an\" checked> Show the curve predicted from peer weight alone</label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"legend\" id=\"do-legend\"></div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-dose\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Detection by number of replaced peers\"></div>\n    <h4>On real development data</h4>\n    <p class=\"note\">Concordance within sentences, by the share of peer weight held by clusters with the wrong meaning (6,772 faithful × unfaithful pairs in 508 sentences, development configuration).</p>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-real\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Within-sentence concordance by wrong-cluster weight share\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"do-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"card view\" id=\"v-legal\">\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:0\">Long legal definitions</h3>\n    <p class=\"q\">Does agreement hold up on text rich in exceptions, where shared error is common?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <label>Exception and condition markers<select id=\"lg-bin\"><option value=\"all\">All 158 sentences</option><option value=\"B0\">0–1 markers</option><option value=\"B1\">2–3 markers</option><option value=\"B2\">4 or more markers</option></select></label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-legal\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Weighted AUROC on the legal set\"></div>\n    <p class=\"note\">Weighted AUROC against panel labels from the sentence alone (no gold exists). These are the weakest labels in the study: Fleiss κ 0.38 overall and 0.17 on sentences with four or more markers.</p>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"lg-take\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <div class=\"prose view\">\n    <h3>What the paper does not show</h3>\n    <ul class=\"limits\">\n      <li><strong>A clear increment.</strong> Added to a base of judge, roundtrip and structural scores, peer agreement gains +0.033 AUROC on panel labels, 95% CI [−0.001, 0.066]. It is significant only under a directional test, on 256 panel items (Kish effective sample size 202).</li>\n      <li><strong>A gain over an existing estimator.</strong> It does not beat binary Dawid–Skene agreement on panel labels (−0.003), and its gain over majority clustering comes from reliability weighting.</li>\n      <li><strong>Human labels.</strong> Panel labels are LLM judgments, with Cohen κ 0.57 against human corrections on MALLS. No human adjudication was used.</li>\n      <li><strong>Every baseline as specified.</strong> Roundtrip baselines on the fresh and legal sets used a local Qwen3-8B back-translation, and the frontier judge was not run on fresh items. GenV, FormalAlign and the relabelling framework of Brunello et al. were not benchmarked.</li>\n      <li><strong>Separation within a sentence.</strong> On development solver labels, shuffling labels within sentences leaves the score at 0.70 AUROC against a true 0.82, so much of its item-level AUROC separates easy sentences from hard ones.</li>\n      <li><strong>Error types.</strong> No reference-free method in the study named real error types better than always predicting the most frequent type.</li>\n      <li><strong>A lone output.</strong> The score needs several independent systems per sentence; with a system's own samples as peers it reduces to self-consistency (0.842 against 0.843).</li>\n    </ul>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n</main>\n\n<!-- ============================================================ FOOTER -->\n<footer id=\"notes\" aria-labelledby=\"h-notes\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-notes\">Links, data and glossary</h2>\n  <ul class=\"links\" aria-label=\"Paper links (repeated)\">\n    <li><a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@main/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a></li>\n    <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@main/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a></li>\n    <li><a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the\">Code repository</a></li>\n  </ul>\n  <h3>Where each view's data comes from</h3>\n  <ul class=\"prov\">\n    <li><strong>The finding, item browser, complexity, stepper, recompute, filter and shared-error views:</strong> <code>experiment_3/method_out.json</code> (4,050 fresh greedy candidates: scores, labels, panel weights, complexity features), joined with <code>experiment_3/work/fresh_frame.jsonl</code> (canonical formulas), <code>experiment_3/results/scores.jsonl</code> (roundtrip scores), <code>experiment_3/work/fresh_dc_weights.json</code> (Dawid–Skene weights) and the pairwise relations in <code>experiment_3/work/pair_cache.jsonl</code>, derived with the run's own <code>dc.align.derive</code> under the frozen configuration. Recomputing every candidate's score from those relations reproduces the recorded score for all 4,050 rows.</li>\n    <li><strong>Confidence intervals on the unfiltered headline chart:</strong> <code>experiment_3/results/tests.json</code>.</li>\n    <li><strong>Renaming test:</strong> <code>experiment_4/results/m1_confound.json</code>.</li>\n    <li><strong>Dose test and real concordance:</strong> <code>experiment_4/results/m3_boundary.json</code>.</li>\n    <li><strong>Legal definitions:</strong> <code>experiment_5/method_out.json</code> (655 panel-labelled candidates with sampling weights).</li>\n  </ul>\n  <p class=\"note\">AUROCs on panel labels are weighted by each item's sampling weight, as in the paper. Where a filter leaves only one label class, the view says so instead of drawing a value. URL = "file:///ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_ue8FYCZb7dRT/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/paper/interactive.html"
```
def run(w, touch=False):

        pg.goto(URL); pg.wait_for_timeout(500)
        T = lambda sel: pg.inner_text(sel)
        def chk(name, sel, act):
            before = T(sel); act(); pg.wait_for_timeout(120); after = T(sel)
            print(f"[{w}] {name}: {'CHANGED' if before != after else 'SAME'} -> {after[:150]}")
        tapper = (lambda loc: loc.tap()) if touch else (lambda loc: loc.click())
        # headline
        chk("head solver", "#head-take", lambda: tapper(pg.locator("#head-fam button[data-v=S]")))
        chk("head corpus", "#head-take", lambda: pg.select_option("#head-corpus", "folio"))
        chk("head terc", "#head-take", lambda: pg.select_option("#head-terc", "top"))
        pg.locator("#v-head").screenshot(path=f"shots/op_{w}_head.png")
        # chart mark tip
        mk = pg.locator("#c-head .mark").first; mk.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
        if touch: mk.tap()
        else: mk.hover()
        pg.wait_for_timeout(100); print(f"[{w}] mark tip visible:", pg.is_visible("#charttip"), T("#charttip")[:80])
        pg.screenshot(path=f"shots/op_{w}_tip.png")
        pg.select_option("#head-corpus", "all"); pg.select_option("#head-terc", "all")
        # term
        term = pg.locator("#finding button.term[data-term=auroc]"); term.scroll_into_view_if_needed()
        tapper(term); pg.wait_for_timeout(200)
        print(f"[{w}] term after click visible:", pg.is_visible("#termtip"), T("#termtip")[:60])
        pg.screenshot(path=f"shots/op_{w}_term.png")
        pg.keyboard.press("Escape"); pg.wait_for_timeout(50); print(f"[{w}] term after Esc visible:", pg.is_visible("#termtip"))
        tapper(term); pg.wait_for_timeout(100)
        tapper(pg.locator("#finding h2")); pg.wait_for_timeout(100); print(f"[{w}] term after outside tap visible:", pg.is_visible("#termtip"))
        # stepper
        for i in range(5):
            chk(f"stepper next {i}", "#st-take", lambda: tapper(pg.locator("#st-next")))
```

```
from pathlib import Path
P = Path("/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_ue8FYCZb7dRT/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/paper")
page = (P/"interactive.html").read_text()

# external refs
refs = re.findall(r'(?:src|href)="([^"]+)"', page)
print("refs:", sorted(set(refs)))
print("link tags/external scripts:", re.findall(r'<link[^>]*>|<script[^>]+src=', page))
for r in refs:
    if r.startswith("figures/"): print(r, "exists:", (P/r).exists())

     "https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the",
     "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-abf543-do-sentence-and-formula-generalize-the@main/report.pdf"}
print("links ok:", {r for r in refs if r.startswith("http")} == L)
# prose = static markup outside script/style
body = re.sub(r"<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>", " ", page, flags=re.S)
prose = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body))
# plus strings in JS that are prose: GLOSS definitions and takeaways templates
js = re.search(r'<script>\n"use strict";(.*)</script>', page, re.S).group(1)
gl = " ".join(re.findall(r'\["[^"]+", "([^"]+)"\]', js))
text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", prose + " " + gl)
words = len(re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", text))
print("words", words, "em dashes", text.count("—"), "per1000", round(1000*text.count("—")/words, 2))
banned = ["delve","underscore","showcase","intricate","pivotal","realm","commendable","meticulous","tapestry","garner","multifaceted","it is worth noting","plays a crucial role","not only"]
print("banned:", [b for b in banned if b in text.lower()], [b for b in banned if b in js.lower()])
hedges = re.findall(r"\b(may|might|likely|suggests?|appears?|perhaps|possibly|could)\b", text, re.I)
print("hedges", len(hedges), hedges, "per1000", round(1000*len(hedges)/words, 2))
sents = [s for s in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", text) if len(s.split()) > 2]
lens = sorted(len(s.split()) for s in sents)
q = statistics.quantiles(lens, n=4); print("sentence IQR", q[2]-q[0], q)
# numbers in static prose vs paper
nums = set(re.findall(r"(?<![\w.])[−+-]?\d[\d,]*\.?\d*%?", prose))
texn = tex.replace("{,}", ",")
miss = [n for n in sorted(nums) if n.strip("−+-%").rstrip(".") not in texn]
print("prose numbers not in paper.tex:", miss)
EOF
```

```
I built `interactive.html` in the paper folder: one 1.75 MB file with all its CSS, JavaScript and data inline. It makes no network requests, and its only image is the method diagram, `figures/fig2_v0.jpg`. I tested it in headless Chromium at 390px with touch and at 1440px, using real clicks and taps on every control. The console showed no errors and the page never scrolled sideways.

**The data is the run's own.** A script reads the output files of experiments 3, 4 and 5 and writes the five JSON blocks the page embeds. The page's live recomputation gives the paper's numbers:
- Peer agreement against the judge is 0.827 vs 0.791 on panel labels and 0.874 vs 0.727 on solver labels.
- When most systems share an error, agreement drops to 0.419 while the judge holds 0.786.
- On the legal definitions, agreement reaches 0.705 against the judge's 0.927.
- The complexity strata, the dose curve and the renaming test also match.

For the pairwise solver relations I used the run's own derivation code on its recorded cache, so nothing was re-solved. Rebuilding every score from those relations gives the recorded value for all 4,050 fresh candidates.

**What the page has, top to bottom:**
- **Header:** the title, with "Read the paper (PDF)" as the main button beside the report and code links. The paper has no author line, so the page says so in place of one.
- **The finding:** the headline number, plus a bar chart of nine scores with the judge always shown. You can switch between panel and solver labels, and filter by corpus and complexity tercile.
- **How it works:** a six-stage walk through one real sentence ("If a student took CPSC 201 but did not take CPSC 223, they can take CPSC 323."). The judge gives all nine systems' outputs 1.00, but agreement separates them. You can choose which output plays the candidate.
- **Explore the evidence:**
  - An item browser over all 4,050 candidates, with filters, search and sort. The detail panel puts the candidate formula next to what most peers wrote and the audited gold.
  - Reliability by sentence complexity.
  - The renaming test.
- **Try it:**
  - Recompute any candidate's score: untick peers or switch to uniform weights and the score updates. The solver itself isn't rerun; the page uses its recorded relations.
  - A threshold slider comparing how many bad formulas agreement catches against the judge at the same flag rate.
- **Where it fails:**
  - The shared-error split, with a list of the items agreement gets wrong.
  - The dose test.
  - Legal definitions by marker count.
  - The paper's limitations.
- **Footer:** the links again, which file each view comes from, and a glossary.

All three links match the ones you gave exactly. The written text has no em dashes, none of the banned words and no hedges, and every number in it appears in `paper.tex`.

I also added one line to `README.md` describing the new file and changed nothing else in the folder. I didn't render any figures, and the storage manifest needed no changes. The structured result is in `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`.
```
